tables.name: orders
tables.description: Fact table: one row per shipped order line, 2024-01-01 to 2025-12-31. Grain = order_id. Joins to customers, products, and carriers via FK ids. Primary asset for late-delivery analysis: late_delivery is the label the ML pipeline predicts and the KPI operations tracks.

columns.name: order_id
columns.description: Surrogate key, unique per order line; starts at 10000.

columns.name: order_date
columns.description: Date the order was placed, ISO YYYY-MM-DD.

columns.name: shipping_date
columns.description: Date the order was actually delivered = order_date + actual_shipping_days. Leakage for ML (encodes the outcome); fine for SQL reporting.

columns.name: customer_id
columns.description: FK to customers.customer_id.

columns.name: product_id
columns.description: FK to products.product_id.

columns.name: carrier_id
columns.description: FK to carriers.carrier_id — which carrier moved the shipment.

columns.name: shipping_mode
columns.description: Service tier: Same Day, First Class, Second Class, or Standard Class. Determines scheduled_shipping_days (1/2/4/6 respectively).

columns.name: scheduled_shipping_days
columns.description: Promised transit time in days, fixed by shipping_mode: Same Day=1, First Class=2, Second Class=4, Standard Class=6.

columns.name: actual_shipping_days
columns.description: Realized transit time in days. Leakage for ML — together with the schedule it determines the target.

columns.name: late_delivery
columns.description: 1 if actual_shipping_days > scheduled_shipping_days, else 0. The business KPI and the ML target.

columns.name: order_item_quantity
columns.description: Units ordered on the line, 1-5.

columns.name: sales
columns.description: Gross sales value of the line in USD.

columns.name: discount
columns.description: Fractional discount applied, 0.00-0.25.

columns.name: profit
columns.description: Profit on the line in USD; can be negative.

columns.name: market
columns.description: Top level of the geo hierarchy: LATAM, Europe, Pacific Asia, USCA, Africa.

columns.name: order_region
columns.description: Region nested under market (e.g. Western Europe).

columns.name: order_country
columns.description: Destination country nested under order_region.

sampleQueries: SELECT shipping_mode, COUNT(*) AS n_orders, ROUND(AVG(late_delivery), 3) AS late_rate FROM orders GROUP BY shipping_mode ORDER BY late_rate DESC
SELECT c.carrier_name, COUNT(*) AS n_orders, ROUND(AVG(o.late_delivery), 3) AS late_rate FROM orders o JOIN carriers c ON o.carrier_id = c.carrier_id GROUP BY c.carrier_name ORDER BY late_rate DESC
SELECT market, ROUND(SUM(sales), 2) AS total_sales, ROUND(SUM(profit), 2) AS total_profit FROM orders GROUP BY market ORDER BY total_sales DESC

tables.name: customers
tables.description: Dimension: one row per customer. Currently a slim dimension carrying the customer's segment; join from orders.customer_id.

columns.name: customer_id
columns.description: Customer surrogate key; starts at 1000.

columns.name: customer_segment
columns.description: Consumer, Corporate, or Home Office.

sampleQueries: SELECT customer_segment, COUNT(*) AS n_customers FROM customers GROUP BY customer_segment
SELECT cu.customer_segment, ROUND(AVG(o.late_delivery), 3) AS late_rate FROM orders o JOIN customers cu ON o.customer_id = cu.customer_id GROUP BY cu.customer_segment

tables.name: products
tables.description: Dimension: one row per distinct product, with its category. Join from orders.product_id.

columns.name: product_id
columns.description: Product surrogate key assigned during warehouse load.

columns.name: product_name
columns.description: Human-readable product name, unique.

columns.name: category_name
columns.description: One of ~10 product categories (Electronics, Furniture, ...).

sampleQueries: SELECT category_name, COUNT(*) AS n_products FROM products GROUP BY category_name ORDER BY n_products DESC
SELECT p.category_name, ROUND(AVG(o.late_delivery), 3) AS late_rate FROM orders o JOIN products p ON o.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.category_name ORDER BY late_rate DESC

tables.name: carriers
tables.description: Dimension: one row per contracted carrier. Bridges the warehouse to the contracts corpus: contract_file names the governing MSA in data/contracts/, and on_time_sla_pct is the contractual on-time commitment from that MSA — compare it to the observed late rate in orders to find SLA breaches.

columns.name: carrier_id
columns.description: Carrier surrogate key.

columns.name: carrier_name
columns.description: SwiftShip Express, Atlas Freight Co., Pacific Crest Carriers, or NordHaul Logistics.

columns.name: contract_file
columns.description: Filename of the governing contract in data/contracts/ (markdown).

columns.name: on_time_sla_pct
columns.description: Contractual on-time delivery commitment in percent (e.g. 96.0 = 96%).

sampleQueries: SELECT carrier_name, on_time_sla_pct, contract_file FROM carriers ORDER BY on_time_sla_pct DESC

SELECT c.carrier_name, ROUND(100 * (1 - AVG(o.late_delivery)), 1) AS observed_on_time_pct, c.on_time_sla_pct AS contractual_sla_pct FROM carriers c JOIN orders o ON o.carrier_id = c.carrier_id GROUP BY c.carrier_id ORDER BY observed_on_time_pct ASC

glossary.definition: An order whose realized transit time exceeded its promise: actual_shipping_days > scheduled_shipping_days (late_delivery = 1). The central KPI of this project and the ML target.

The contractual minimum percentage of shipments a carrier must deliver on or before the scheduled date in a measurement period; falling below it triggers the penalty/credit clauses of the carrier's contract.
Promised transit time in days, fixed by shipping mode: Same Day=1, First Class=2, Second Class=4, Standard Class=6.
Top level of the geographic hierarchy market > region > country. One of: LATAM, Europe, Pacific Asia, USCA, Africa.
The delivery service tier sold to the customer (Same Day, First Class, Second Class, Standard Class). Tighter modes promise fewer days and are empirically more often late.
The contracted logistics provider that physically moves a shipment. Each carrier has a signed MSA in data/contracts/ governing penalties and SLAs.

The contractual financial remedy owed when a carrier or supplier misses its delivery commitment. Formulas differ by contract (per-day %, flat fee, service credits, liquidated damages) — see the contract_file of the relevant carrier.
